title: Plumas Working Forests — method costs, harvest baseline, and gaps
disclaimer: Absolute figures below are the best public numbers we can cite so far. Confidence grades: A = official CA schedule or county harvest series; B = peer-reviewed or multi-study regional range; C = illustrative placeholder; D = known gap (null). Net owner profit by method is D until local bids and stumpage actuals land. Other agents: fill nulls via program/data/INTAKE.md — do not invent.

confidence_legend.A: Official California schedule or published county harvest series with stable methodology
confidence_legend.B: Peer-reviewed or multi-study Western US / CA range; not Plumas-bid-specific
confidence_legend.C: Illustrative / order-of-magnitude only — not for business decisions
confidence_legend.D: Data gap — value is null or intentionally omitted

geography.tva_note: CDTFA Timber Value Areas follow county lines (with I-5 splits in Shasta/Siskiyou/Tehama). Plumas sits in the interior Sierra TVA band; cite the TVA column used when applying Table G.

plumas_harvest_mbf.source: University of Montana BBER Forest Industry Research — Timber Harvest for Plumas County, California
plumas_harvest_mbf.notes: Private includes industrial + NIPF + tribal where reported; FS = USDA Forest Service. Post-Dixie years (2021–2023) show elevated private salvage/green volume — not a steady-state baseline alone.

stumpage_cdtfa_ihv.source: CDTFA Harvest Values Schedule (Table G green timber), effective 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-30
stumpage_cdtfa_ihv.unit: USD per MBF (immediate harvest value for yield tax — not the same as every private stumpage contract)
stumpage_cdtfa_ihv.notes: Table values assume tractor logging and ≥300 MBF quarter volume. Skyline −$100/MBF; helicopter −$350/MBF; small total volume and low volume/acre deductions apply. Biomass/chips (Table 1 CS) IHV = $0/ton.

table_g_selected.description: Interior Sierra-relevant TVA columns 5–7 (verify county TVA map before using a single column)

cost_line_items.label: Forest thinning operations (Western US literature range)
cost_line_items.year_context: Synthesis cited as Chang et al. 2023 (Western US)
cost_line_items.source: Systematic literature review / synthesis of Western US thinning costs (Chang et al. 2023), as cited in subsequent CA forest-economics papers
cost_line_items.notes: Wide range reflects terrain, volume removed, system (CTL vs whole-tree), and whether biomass is utilized. Not a Plumas contractor bid.

cost_line_items.notes: Often above pure commercial thin cost; used for pace-and-scale funding math, not THP clearcut accounting.

cost_line_items.label: Pile burning (Western US range)

cost_line_items.notes: Stack on top of cutting costs when slash is piled and burned.

cost_line_items.label: CDTFA skyline vs tractor — tax IHV deduction (proxy for higher yard cost)
cost_line_items.notes: Official tax adjustment, not a full logging-rate survey. Signals skyline costs more than tractor.

cost_line_items.label: CDTFA helicopter vs tractor — tax IHV deduction
Broadcast herbicide site-prep / release (chemical free-to-grow)
cost_line_items.notes: GAP: need Plumas/SPI-class contractor bids or published CA industrial silviculture cost tables. Chem is cheap relative to manual — that is why it is common — but absolute $/ac not yet sourced for this ledger.

cost_line_items.label: Manual / mechanical release (no broadcast herbicide)
cost_line_items.notes: GAP: local hand-crew and mastication release bids. Expected higher than chemical; measure the increment for cost-share design.

cost_line_items.label: Planting (seedlings + plant labor)
cost_line_items.notes: GAP: density (TPA), species, and access drive cost. Post-fire units differ from green clearcut.

cost_line_items.label: Clearcut / high-volume regen harvest logging cost
cost_line_items.notes: GAP: local LTO rates. Generally lower $/MBF than partial cut at same site.

cost_line_items.label: Partial cut / commercial thin logging cost
cost_line_items.notes: GAP: local LTO rates. Often higher $/MBF; more acres can still raise total logger revenue.

cost_line_items.label: Mill-delivered log price by sort (pond value)
cost_line_items.notes: GAP: mill quotes. CDTFA IHV is tax value, not delivered log price.

cost_line_items.label: Net revenue to landowner after logging, haul, regen, release
cost_line_items.notes: GAP: the number that decides adoption. Requires filling the lines above.

methods.name: Clearcut / regen harvest → plant → broadcast chemical release
methods.spraymapca_link: Primary driver of mapped forestry herbicides (glyphosate, hexazinone, imazapyr)
known: Produces high MBF/ac at entry when volume is there
Chemical release typically cheapest path to free-to-grow (absolute $/ac still D)
Plumas private harvest MBF known at county scale (not by silvicultural method)
unknown: Share of Plumas MBF that is this pathway vs thin
loss_risks: Watershed chemical load (non-market; see site Science tab)

methods.name: Clearcut / regen harvest → plant → mechanical/manual release only
methods.spraymapca_link: Would cut mapped spray if substituted at scale
known: Same harvest entry economics as chemical path until release step
Release step expected more expensive than chemical (magnitude D)
unknown: Stocking success rates without spray on Plumas sites
loss_risks: Higher cash cost of free-to-grow if no cost-share

methods.name: Working forest: VDT matrix + small gaps + multi-entry (no broadcast spray)
methods.spraymapca_link: Designed for zero broadcast free-to-grow under Standard
known: Partial-cut logging often higher $/MBF (signaled by CDTFA skyline/heli deductions)
Can return volume on shorter cycles; parity unproven for Plumas (T1)
unknown: Mill sort acceptance for thin mix
loss_risks: If T1 fails: lower decade MBF (a real industrial loss)
If offtake fails: stranded small wood

methods.name: Fuels / restoration thin (public-funded, utilization when possible)
methods.spraymapca_link: May or may not include herbicide depending on project design
known: Thin subset may fall in Western $307–$1,737/ac band before pile burn
unknown: Plumas NF unit-level actuals from FACTS + contracts
loss_risks: Without utilization, public pays full cost; with utilization, commercial revenue offsets
